JOH Opera House · Parts 004 & 005 · Vertical transport

OTIS lifts L12, L15–L23: site readiness for installation handover

What has to be in place in each shaft before OTIS can take it over and start installing. It covers ten lifts, their approved shop drawings, the structural and architectural references, a checklist for the walk-down, and the open issues with the way to close each one. Issued 02 Nov 2026. Sources: approved OTIS shop drawings (Code B), structural core-wall drawings, TQ log and CRS comments.

Lift-specific points

  • Fire-fighters’ lift. Feed from the generator-backed panel (MCC/M/3/LS1) and size cables and equipment for it. (TQ-953)
  • Guide-rail lateral support: concrete stiffener beams were reviewed with comments. Resubmit and build them before rails are fixed. (TQ-1116)
  • E&I panel recess 350×1750×115 with 350×140 opening below in core C4.01 at L06. Show it on the shop drawing before breaking out. (TQ-1287)
  • Pit is in the TQ-1379 list: fill the extra depth with C5 concrete or compacted soil to 1600 mm, per the K&A comments. (TQ-1379)
  • Longest travel in the group (≈34.9 m). Run a full-height plumb survey before rails are ordered to length.

Lift-specific points

  • Pit depth 1800 mm, the only pit in this group that is not 1600.
  • MBL owes a method statement for filling gaps and correcting the rough door openings. Signage on this lift is by MBL.
  • Plan the delivery route and lifting for the heavy machine and rails. The car is 2400 × 3500.

Site status

Site preparation for handover to OTIS

Numbers on each drawing match the notes beside it.

Shaft – pit to top slab

  1. 1Top slab cast and closed; clear overhead from top FFL to slab soffit 5300–5400 (min. 4600, TQ-952).
  2. 2Hook beam / lifting point under the top slab, SWL marked and load-tested (CAL-CIV-0016).
  3. 3Isolator and power point at the top level, labelled.
  4. 4Shaft lighting along the full height (ICAD); temporary lights until then.
  5. 5Plumb line / laser survey top to pit; report handed to OTIS before rails are cut.
  6. 6Guide-rail bracket lines on solid concrete or approved stiffener beams – no brackets on blockwork.
  7. 7Landing opening at every stop, sized to OTIS.
  8. 8FFL datum and 1 m mark at every landing.
  9. 9Shaft empty: no scaffolding, props, boards or debris; no other trade inside.
  10. 10Pit floor 1600 below the lowest FFL (L17 1800); extra depth filled per TQ-1379.
  11. 11Pit dry and waterproofed; sump kept with open grating (TQ-66); ladder zone clear.

Landing – front view

  1. 1Rough opening W × H measured from FFL and signed by OTIS; gaps over 100 mm filled with blockwork (PRP-0051).
  2. 2Call-button recess 600×300×50 beside the door; indicator recess 400×150×50 above (TQ-544).
  3. 31 m mark: line exactly 1000 above finished floor level.
  4. 4Temporary DB near the landing for OTIS tools and lights.
  5. 5Rigid barrier 1.1 m high with mid rail and toe board, fixed to the jambs.
  6. 6HBP hole in the slab beside the door: Ø50 (Ø40 at G, B1, B2).
  7. 7Area in front of the landing clear for work and material delivery.

Rigid edge protection at each open landing

  1. 1Top rail at 1100 above FFL, fixed into the jambs (not leaning on blockwork).
  2. 2Mid rail at about 500.
  3. 3Toe board 150 high, tight to the sill.
  4. 4Mesh or board infill so nothing falls into the shaft.
  5. 5Sign: DANGER – LIFT SHAFT, do not remove. Barrier stays until OTIS takes over that landing.

Survey setting-out
S1FFL marked with a 1 m datum line at every landing.
S2Shaft centre lines and reference lines marked at the pit and the top level.
Structure and blockwork
T1Core walls complete; no formwork, ties or bar ends inside the shaft.
T2Top slab cast and closed over the shaft.
T3Hook beam installed, SWL marked and load-tested (CAL-CIV-0016).
T4Pit floor at the required depth (1600, L17 1800); extra depth filled.
T5Pit dry and waterproofed; sump with open grating.
T6Landing openings built to OTIS size; jambs and gaps finished (PRP-0051).
As-built survey
M1Plumb survey of the shaft, top to pit, report handed to OTIS.
M2Hoistway W × D at every level not less than the OTIS size.
M3Pit depth and overhead measured and accepted by OTIS.
M4Opening W × H at every landing measured and signed by OTIS.
Scaffolding and logistics
L1Scaffolding installed in the shaft.
L2Material route to the shaft and a lockable store nearby.
L3Temporary power at pit and top level, and temporary lighting in the shaft.
Safety
F1Rigid barrier 1.1 m with mid rail and toe board at every open landing.
F2DANGER – LIFT SHAFT sign and controlled access at every landing.
F3Safe access into the pit (ladder) and no water in the pit.
